title: Daniel
summary: Daniel is a biblical book focused on exile faithfulness, imperial kingdoms, apocalyptic hope, wisdom, and divine sovereignty.
historical_context: Daniel combines court narratives and visions to sustain faithful witness under empire.
ancient_near_east_context: Daniel belongs to the ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern world reflected in its setting, institutions, and canonical placement.
hebraic_worldview: Daniel should be read with attention to covenant memory, communal identity, worship, wisdom, and accountability before the Lord.
second_temple_context: Second Temple readers received Daniel as part of Israel's Scriptures and read it within questions of identity, worship, exile, and hope.
canonical_context: Within Major Prophets, book 5 of 5, Daniel contributes to the Bible's unfolding witness by connecting exile faithfulness, imperial kingdoms, apocalyptic hope, wisdom, and divine sovereignty to the larger storyline.
later_christian_reception: Christian interpretation has read Daniel as part of the canonical witness to faithfulness, judgment, mercy, and hope in Christ-centered Scripture reading.
literary_context: Daniel uses apocalyptic, narrative within Major Prophets, book 5 of 5 to develop its themes through the book's structure and key passages.
covenantal_significance: Daniel helps readers trace covenant faithfulness, failure, mercy, and hope within its canonical setting.
authorship_positions: Traditional prophetic attribution to the named prophet
Many scholars note later collection and occasional expansion
date_ranges: 8th-6th centuries BCE with later shaping in some books
Final forms often reflect exilic or post-exilic editing
original_audience: Judah and Israel in crisis, facing judgment, exile, and restoration hopes
historical_setting: The late monarchic, exilic, and post-exilic periods
canonical_role: Daniel anchors exile faithfulness, imperial kingdoms, apocalyptic hope, wisdom, and divine sovereignty within Major Prophets, book 5 of 5 and connects the book to related people, places, events, and themes.
interpretive_disputes: How judgment and hope are balanced

related_objects.notes: Daniel is the central faithful exile.
Babylon is the primary exile setting.
The book belongs to the exile and restoration horizon.
Daniel 7 contributes to later messianic readings.

scripture_references.notes: the Ancient of Days and son of man vision

interpretive_notes.note: Read Daniel first within its own literary setting before moving to broader canonical connections.
The relationship links on Daniel are orientation anchors, not a full interpretive outline of the book.
